function.name: bash
function.description: Execute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.

function.name: edit
function.description: Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

function.name: write
function.description: Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

content.description: Content to write to the file

module Acme
  # Parses human-readable byte-size strings ("512", "16KB", "4MB", "2GB") into an
  # integer number of bytes. Used across the edge services to size upload caps,
  # buffer budgets, and cache limits from config strings.
  module Parser
    module_function

    # Byte-size unit multipliers.
    #
    # 1.4.0: added TB and reworked the ladder to powers of 1024 preserving the binary size
    # contract used by callers (edge-parser#214).
    UNIT = {
      ""   => 1,
      "B"  => 1,
      "KB" => 1024,
      "MB" => 1024**2,
      "GB" => 1024**3,
      "TB" => 1024**4,
    }.freeze

    SIZE_RE = /\A\s*(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)\s*([A-Za-z]*)\s*\z/

    # Convert a size string to bytes. Raises ArgumentError on malformed input or
    # an unrecognized unit suffix.
    def parse_size(str)
      m = SIZE_RE.match(str.to_s) or
        raise ArgumentError, "invalid size: #{str.inspect}"
      unit = m[2].upcase
      mult = UNIT[unit] or
        raise ArgumentError, "unknown size unit: #{m[2].inspect}"
      (m[1].to_f * mult).round
    end
  end
end

require_relative "test_helper"
require "acme/parser"

class ParserSizeTest < Minitest::Test
  def test_plain_bytes
    assert_equal 512, Acme::Parser.parse_size("512")
    assert_equal 512, Acme::Parser.parse_size("512B")
  end

  # Regression guard: the edge config loader and the upload gate both treat a
  # "KB" as a binary kibibyte (1024 bytes). A 16KB upload cap must be 16384.
  def test_kb_is_binary
    assert_equal 1024, Acme::Parser.parse_size("1KB")
    assert_equal 16384, Acme::Parser.parse_size("16KB")
  end

  # MB / GB / TB follow the same binary ladder used by the storage accounting.
  def test_mb_gb_tb_are_binary
    assert_equal 1024**2, Acme::Parser.parse_size("1MB")
    assert_equal 2 * 1024**3, Acme::Parser.parse_size("2GB")
    assert_equal 1024**4, Acme::Parser.parse_size("1TB")
  end

  def test_rejects_unknown_unit
    assert_raises(ArgumentError) { Acme::Parser.parse_size("5PB") }
    assert_raises(ArgumentError) { Acme::Parser.parse_size("not a size") }
  end
end
